title: A protected night repositioning round to reduce hospital-acquired pressure injuries on two medical wards: a quality improvement project
abstract: Problem: 41 category 2 or worse pressure injuries in a year on two medical wards, most found after night shifts, with poor night staffing on almost half of nights. Intervention: a protected night repositioning round with handover risk reassessment, a float nurse when available and touch-based skin assessment, tested in three PDSA cycles. Measures: patient-days between injuries found at weekly inspection, rates by night staffing, round completion and balancing measures. Results will follow the cycles.
introduction: Night staffing is associated with pressure injuries, and protected repositioning has been followed by fewer injuries in an uncontrolled report. The multicentre ratio study quoted locally could not be traced by the recorded search.
methods: Model for Improvement; three PDSA cycles from November 2026 to April 2027; outcome from weekly skin inspection with a fixed counting rule; g-chart with pre-specified rules; registration QI-2026-054.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the g-chart, staffing-stratified rates, round completion and balancing measures, with injuries by skin tone category.
discussion: The discussion will interpret any signal against co-interventions, state what the project shows about poorly staffed nights, and avoid causal claims about staffing ratios.
limitations: Two wards; uncontrolled; rare events; float nurse availability outside the team's control.
conclusion: To be written after the cycles; limited to these wards' injuries and the round's delivery.
summary: SQUIRE-structured draft with results left empty.
